findings.evidence: The roadmap README line 248 explicitly requires `indFDRep : FDRep k S ⥤ FDRep k G`; the declaration at lines 176–183 instead has type `FDRep k S → FDRep k G`, and line 187 provides only an objectwise isomorphism.
findings.fix: Define `indFDRep : FDRep k S ⥤ FDRep k G` (with its morphism map) and state the forgetful compatibility as a natural isomorphism.
findings.issue: `indFDRep` is only an object-level function, so it cannot map intertwiners or support the later categorical induction API.

findings.evidence: Lines 114–126 characterize both directions of `coindSubtypeEquivPi`, but lines 131–147 define `indSubtypeEquivPi` with no corresponding lemmas; the roadmap README lines 245–249 says this named equivalence powers the character formula and Mackey splitting.
findings.fix: Add `[simp]` application and inverse-application lemmas expressing the maps through `Rep.indCoindIso` and `coindSubtypeEquivPi` (and expose any induced-action coordinate formula needed downstream).
findings.issue: The reusable `indSubtypeEquivPi` is opaque and has no forward or inverse application lemmas, so consumers cannot use its coset coordinates without unfolding its implementation.

summary: The public API omits the functorial induction required by the roadmap and does not characterize the named induction–coset equivalence. These gaps prevent later character and categorical results from using the construction abstractly.
